MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  BUDGET STUDY SESSION
  JUNE 8, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 5:10 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Kane Thuyen
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Levi Sinkler

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

5.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022 BUDGET STUDY SESSION

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the information and discuss the
  programs and services to allow staff to prepare the final budget for presentation and
  public hearing on June 22, 2021.
  1
ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JUNE 8, 2021
 City Manager Grammer introduced the Fiscal Year 2021-2022 proposed budget, and
provided an overview. He stated that this year’s budget reflects increased revenues from
building permits, increased revenue resulting from property tax, and a slight increase in sales
tax. The current year has ended with $3.1 million in building permits, much better than
expected addition to revenue that allowed for a projected year-end surplus of about 15%.
Revenue estimates were very conservative, with the unknown in the building industry going
into a pandemic. Businesses were closing down leaving the City with uncertainty when
projecting sales tax revenue. However, the year is ending with projected revenues of over
one million dollars in sales tax which demonstrates how strong our business community has
been at adapting to the changing environment over the last year. The proposed budget
includes maintenance of essential services with increases in areas such as tree trimming.
The Community Grant Program for community groups and nonprofits who wish to apply for
funds has also been reinstated. There will be funding of nearly $800,000 in street resurfacing
projects combining general funds and restricted funds as well as $400,000 in for storm drain
projects. Staff has obtained a number of grant funds for projects that will be implemented
next year or the following year, including $1.5 million from Measure M sub-regional funds,
for traffic signal improvements at Dapplegray School. Additionally there are a number of
grant funds, specific to the General Plan Update and funding for George F Canyon Nature
Center.

Administrative Services Director, Mike Whitehead, provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material), and presented the proposed budget.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN pointed out that the City’s decision to maintain 25% in reserves is
not arbitrary and is based on recommendations of a consultant that follows specific
government finance best practices.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA concurred with Mayor Zuckerman’s point regarding the
level of reserve. She indicated that she initially thought it was not enough, based on previous
positions on the school board, but after serving on the budget subcommittee, found that the
City is above the recommended reserve percentage.

City Manager Grammer noted that staff will return later this summer with a proposed
expenditure plan for the American Rescue Plan Act for the City Council to review, provide
input, and approve how to spend the $1.9 million in monies. The allocation, provided by the
Federal Government to non-entitlement cities, or small cities under 80,000 population, is
higher than the amount anticipated a few months ago. He noted existing restrictions on how
the funds can be spent with respect to infrastructure projects, noting they are limited between
areas of broadband, sewer and water. He added that staff if looking closely to see if there is
an ability to use the funds for potential storm drain repair projects. Once the expenditures
are approved, the budget will be amended accordingly.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN pointed out that there is no additional funding for the Junior
Naturalist position through the Palos Verdes Land Conservancy (PVLC) and Administrative
Services Director Whitehead explained this was a pass-through grant and that the City acted
as an intermediary for the PVLC to receive the funds. Immediately after receiving the grant
funds, the City issued a check to the Land Conservancy in the amount of the awarded grant.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA pointed out that the special revenue section of the budget
is enhanced due to the hard work of staff seeking grant opportunities. Director Whitehead
concurred noting that staff looks for every opportunity to obtain grants, adding that staff
applies for many, some of which are not approved or accepted and many that are, as shown
by parks grants. City Manager Grammer stated that collaboration with other agencies and
other cites is instrumental in obtaining grants.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ commended and thanked Planning Manager Naughton
whom she believes went far and beyond on General Plan grant opportunities noting that one
submission yielded more money than was applied for due to the quality of the grant
submission.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 8, 2021
 Discussion ensued regarding circumstances of anticipated grant funds that are never
received and how staff deals with those instances.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired on the Budget in Brief and requested that a salary and
benefits graph be included.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired regarding adding a list of some City contracts and City
Manager Grammer concurred, adding that some essential service items will be included
for the public’s benefit.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired about CalPERS liabilities and Director Whitehead noted
that RHE is approximately 80% funded. He detailed the strategies followed to meet that
funded level He also noted the lower PEPRA rate tier and employee’s contributions,
pointing out that as the Classic tier membership decreases and new employees join the
City, PEPRA membership increases, reducing PERS costs.

  CITY COUNCIL REVIEWED THE INFORMATION AND DISCUSSED THE
  PROGRAMS AND SERVICES TO ALLOW STAFF TO PREPARE THE
  FINAL BUDGET FOR PRESENTATION AND PUBLIC HEARING ON JUNE
  22, 2021.

6.  ADJOURNMENT

At 6:15 P.M. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting to the Regular City
Council meeting at 7:00 pm.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Carrie Gallagher, CMC  Steve Zuckerman
Interim City Clerk  Mayor

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 8, 2021
